about: Strawberry: why AI couldn't count the r's in strawberry. Part 2 of the AI-explained series after Next word. Narration-led: the voice is recorded first and every visual beat is keyed to its word times.

lines.text: How many r's in strawberry? ChatGPT used to say two.
lines.say: How many R's in strawberry? ChatGPT used to say two.

lines.text: Even when you asked, are you sure? Two.
lines.say: Even when you asked, are you sure? Two!

lines.text: So how does a machine this smart miss a letter?
lines.say: So how does a machine this smart, miss a letter?

lines.text: Because it never sees letters. It sees tokens.
And in your question, strawberry is a single token.
To the model, the whole word is just one number.
lines.say: To the model, the whole word is just, one number.

lines.text: No s, no t, no r's. Nothing inside to count.
lines.say: No S. No T. No R's. Nothing inside to count.

lines.text: But here's the twist. It knows how strawberry is spelled.
So it spells and counts in its head, all in one go.
And repeated letters are exactly where models slip.
It even said straw has one, berry has two. Total? Two.
Now watch the fix. Spell it out, with spaces.
Every letter becomes its own token. Three r's, in plain sight.
lines.say: Every letter becomes its own token. Three R's, in plain sight.

lines.text: Newer thinking models spell it first, or run a little code.
And yes, OpenAI's first thinking model was codenamed Strawberry.
By 2025, most chatbots got strawberry right. But it's not gone.
lines.say: By twenty twenty-five, most chatbots got strawberry right. But it's not gone.

lines.text: In 2025, a brand-new GPT-5 told someone blueberry has three b's.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-five, a brand-new G P T five told someone blueberry has three B's.

lines.text: Same blindness. Blueberry is one token too.
It's not that it can't count. It can't see what it's counting.
